beats.say: A coding agent writes a small parser for a test report. Watch the first case. The parser looks up status in its attributes and stops with a KeyError.
Here is the case that stopped it. Would you inspect the class name, the name of the test, or the elements inside the case? Look for the evidence that tells you whether this test failed.
Inside the case there is a failure element. The traceback names the missing key. Together those clues give us a change to test. Keep the report fixed while we change the lookup.

With the host user's authority, that process could reach other files and network routes. For the next attempt the supervisor supplies this report and a scratch volume. It limits file access, network access and resources outside the candidate. Only a bounded account of the run comes back for the next repair.

title: Which cases earn an output row?

beats.say: Start with a contract. For this fixture, report failed or errored tests as class and name, keep first-seen order, and remove duplicate pairs. The root namespace tells us which report tags to recognize.

The failing run gives us the command, exit code one, and the exact exception. Limit stdout and stderr in bytes as you collect them. Even one line can be enormous. Keep useful beginning and ending excerpts, escape control characters, and treat the text as data. Cap retries and diagnose repeated failures before changing permissions.
Now run the repair on those four cases. Read the direct children of each case. Keep the first failure. Drop its duplicate. Keep the error. Skip the last case. Read back the two names in the output.

The two rows are rejects failure and handles error, both in the report parser class. A direct skipped child wins even beside an error. Match the root namespace and check that the child exists. An empty failure element still counts.

Reject a selected case with a blank class or name, and reject malformed XML. Bound the input, its decompressed size, parsing time and memory. This contract covers our fixtures. Another report producer needs its own cases.

title: Who can issue a passing receipt?

beats.say: The supervisor freezes the parser files and owns setup, the repair loop and the deadline. Inside the worker, the candidate and its dependencies can change their own interpreter. A read-only test file still leaves its assertions in that shared process.
Suppose a faulty run exits zero and returns an empty list. Follow that answer across the boundary. The validator outside the worker holds the two expected rows. Do the results match?
They differ. The validator rejects the empty list even though the process exited zero. Try the repaired parser on exactly the same report. Keep your eye on the expected rows.

Here come the two repaired rows. The validator compares their values and order. They match. The supervisor keeps the passing verdict in a protected record. A transferable receipt needs an authenticated validator, with its signing key outside the worker.
The receipt binds the job, base revision, file bytes, image, dependencies and grader. At acceptance the image changes from I seven to I eight. Can we use the recorded pass?
Retest on I eight. The record still describes I seven. Its digest lets a trusted checker detect changed bytes. A digest alone cannot tell us who issued the verdict.
A temporary working directory and an empty environment look tidy. Our benign absolute-path probe can still read notes.txt. What did we learn about networking?

Network access is unmeasured. The empty environment removed inherited variables. The working directory changed how relative names resolve. The operating system still granted that file read. Now give four example runtimes the same read-only report and trace the grant.

In this container a scoped mount exposes report.xml. The process shares the host kernel. Namespaces shape its view, capabilities and syscall filters limit operations, and cgroups limit resources. Mounts, devices and daemon access change the effective boundary.

With gVisor, the Sentry mediates many application system calls. This configuration uses a Gofer for the file read. A Firecracker microVM reads an attached volume through its own guest kernel and a virtual machine monitor over KVM. Host device and network policy still matter.

WebAssembly checks guest memory and control flow. This worker gets a host import for one report handle. The other three get the same file by different routes. Now request notes.txt in these four scoped configurations. Which grant covers it?

All four refuse that read. Real choices depend on the workload, compatible calls, and the rights you actually grant. Measure time until the job can run, including setup. Then probe the configuration you plan to use.

title: What did this control actually stop?

beats.say: Our offline worker needs one schema. In preparation, fetch a pinned artifact through limited egress. The first copy has a different digest. Keep it out. Fetch the pinned copy. Its digest matches the trusted lockfile. Admit those bytes to the cache. A matching digest identifies the bytes. Build scripts still run untrusted code. Keep the builder scoped and free of production credentials.

Run the worker with the approved cache and outbound networking blocked. A probe records an enforced denial. Now suppose the environment contains a synthetic marker called AMBER. The worker writes it into its returned file. Which control held?

Network denial held. The marker left through the artifact. Keep unnecessary credentials outside both jobs. Scrubbing logs can miss an encoded value. These observations tell us nothing about parser correctness.

Fill a sixty-four mebibyte scratch volume. One extra write fails. At a limit of sixty-four tasks, a new task is refused. Existing tasks can keep running. Limit returned bytes, host logs, memory and total concurrent jobs as well.

Now watch two runnable threads share thirty milliseconds of CPU time per hundred milliseconds. One uses twenty, the other ten. The quota is spent. Across the job that is three tenths of one logical CPU. The budget renews next period.

Does renewal extend the job's life? The separate supervisor clock keeps counting, even while threads wait. At three seconds of wall time its deadline expires. It starts whole-job teardown. We still need to see what stopped.

title: Who is still drawing the fish?

beats.say: Watch the tail on the scratch disk in slot A. This is run seven. Cancel the parent. Its process has exited. Can you see who is still painting?
The helper is still writing orange pixels. A cancellation request reaches the supervisor before it has evidence that every process is gone. Could we give this slot to another job yet?
Hold the slot. The supervisor stops the whole job through its runtime and verifies zero live processes. The orange stripe stops here. What still belongs to run seven?
The fish is a file. Scratch is the only writable storage for this job. Replace the scratch volume. Verify it is empty. Only now can the supervisor admit another worker.
Run eight gets the empty volume and starts a blue ray. A delayed cleanup record arrives for seven. Which worker does the record name?

It names worker seven. Address that immutable worker ID and guard slot updates by lease generation. Eight keeps painting. Store the ID, generation and lifetime outside the worker so an independent reaper can retry after a supervisor failure. If termination or reset stays uncertain, quarantine the slot.

title: Where does the guest boundary end?

beats.say: Give this WebAssembly guest one typed function, run, from a signed thirty-two-bit integer to an integer of the same type. The host checks the signature and rejects imports in this example. Give its add-one function forty-one. It returns forty-two. Change just the argument to the largest signed integer. Adding one wraps to the smallest signed integer in thirty-two bits.

Enable Wasmtime fuel metering and set the budget before instantiation, because a start function can run there. Picture a toy trace charging one unit per step. It needs one hundred thirty-two steps. The hundred-unit budget runs out. The next step traps.

Fuel meters guest work. Compilation, host calls and host allocations need separate limits and an outside deadline. Now look at a different limit. One memory page is already allocated. The highest valid byte is sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-five.
A four-byte load at address sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-two fits. Slide the start two bytes to the right. Does the same load fit now?
The load traps. Its last two bytes land outside the page. Separately, request a second page under a one-page limit. Growth returns minus one to the guest. The existing page stays in place.

Suppose a different host links a file reader. A file name can resolve through an alias to another resource. The host must check the actual resource at open time against a scoped grant. Here only the report handle is granted. The notes file stays outside it.

title: Which results can we carry forward?

beats.say: Functional tests ask whether a patch matches expected behavior. Containment probes ask whether the runtime enforces its access and resource boundaries. In this fixed pool of five candidates, two pass the parser fixture. Pick two different indices uniformly. How many pairs contain a pass?

There are ten possible pairs. Three pairs contain only failures. Seven out of ten contain a passing candidate, so pass at two is seventy percent for this pool. Count candidate indices even if the code repeats. Drawing with replacement would describe a different experiment.
Add one more failing candidate. Two of six now pass. Count all the pairs that contain only failures, then take the complement. What fraction contain a pass?

Six of fifteen pairs miss both passing candidates. Nine out of fifteen succeed, or sixty percent. For model comparisons, keep tasks, budgets and graders fixed. Successive repairs respond to earlier feedback. Sample independent whole repair trajectories when estimating success across runs.

Try the frozen parser on a fresh namespaced report. All four cases have the class name payments. Retry has a direct failure and error. Later has skipped and error. Nested has a failure under details. Retry appears again. Predict the ordered output.

Only payments, retry appears, once. Class and name make one identity. The skipped case drops out, the nested failure is too deep, and the repeat adds no new identity. The validator records this functional pass for the tested artifact and environment.

One last decision. The independent network probe recorded a deny, and teardown verified zero live processes. The scratch volume still holds one file. Would you accept the parser result for review? Would you admit a new job to this slot?

Keep the parser result for review. Hold the slot until reset is verified. The receipt tells you which patch passed which checks. The deny record describes that network probe. The leftover file tells you why the next job must wait.
